headline_marked: Parliament [[passes law to replace RAB with SRB]]
headline: Parliament passes law to replace RAB with SRB
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) will be a specialized unit under the police, aimed at combating terrorism and organized crime.
details: The National Parliament has passed the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' via voice vote on Thursday, September 10. The law mandates the dissolution of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and the creation of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as a specialized unit under the police.

The bill was moved by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed during the third session of the 13th National Parliament. It had previously been sent to a parliamentary committee for scrutiny after being introduced on September 3, with the report being presented by Chief Whip Nurul Islam Mani on Wednesday.

Opposition members raised seven objections, arguing that a stronger accountability mechanism and national consultation were needed before replacing RAB. Their concerns included the speed of the bill's passage, the direct transfer of RAB's manpower and assets to SRB, and the framework for investigating complaints.

The government stated that a modern, professional, and accountable specialized unit is necessary to protect public security, combat terrorism, and organized crime. The SRB will be headquartered in Dhaka and will be ensure transparency and effective oversight in the power of its operations.

The unit will be composed of officers and armed personnel from the police and other disciplinary forces as needed. It will be led by a Director General, who will be appointed from among officers of at least Additional Inspector General of Police rank from the Bangladesh Police.
caption:

headline_marked: Tk 666 crore tax: [[Grameen Kalyan loses HC petitions]] over reassessment
headline: Tk 666 crore tax: Grameen Kalyan loses HC petitions over reassessment
summary: The High Court has rejected challenges by the non-profit founded by Professor Muhammad Yunus against NBR tax orders.
details: The High Court has rejected two petitions filed by Grameen Kalyan, a non-profit and charitable organisation founded by Nobel laureate and former chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus.
The court's decision upholds the National Board of Revenue (NBR) orders to reassess income tax for several tax years, involving a total of approximately Tk 666 crore.
Deputy Attorney General Abdus Samad Azad stated that the NBR will issue a notice to the organisation seeking the tax amount for the period between 2012-13 and 2016-17.
The verdict was delivered by a bench of Justice Md Mozibur Rahman Miah and Justice Rezaul Karim.
Barrister Abdullah Al Mamun, representing Grameen Kalyan, announced that the organisation will appeal the High Court's verdict before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court.
The lawyer added that if the Appellate Division grants a stay on the verdict, Grameen Kalyan will not be required to pay the claimed amount.
caption:
A non-profit founded by Professor Muhammad Yunus must pay Tk 666 crore in tax after the High Court rejected its petitions.

The High Court has rejected two petitions filed by Grameen Kalyan, a non-profit and charitable organisation founded by Nobel laureate and former chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus.

The court's decision upholds the National Board of Revenue (NBR) orders to reassess income tax for several tax years, involving a total of approximately Tk 666 crore.

Deputy Attorney General Abdus Samad Azad stated that the NBR will issue a notice to the organisation seeking the tax amount for the period between 2012-13 and 2016-17.

The verdict was delivered by a bench of Justice Md Mozibur Rahman Miah and Justice Rezaul Karim.

Barrister Abdullah Al Mamun, representing Grameen Kalyan, announced that the organisation will appeal the High Court's verdict before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court.

The lawyer added that if the Appellate Division grants a stay on the verdict, Grameen Kalyan will not be required to pay the claimed amount.
